data.title: AFDB's flat .cif objects are unreadable through object_store, at scan time and read time
data.body:
Blocks the cheapest way to build an AFDB catalog. Tracking here so it gets re-tested when upstream moves; nothing to fix in this repo.

## What happens

Every `AF-*.cif` at the root of `gs://public-datasets-deepmind-alphafold-v4` is stored with `Content-Encoding: gzip`. GCS transcodes on read, omits `Content-Length`, and the Rust `object_store` crate treats that as fatal:

```
Generic GCS error: Content-Length Header missing from response
```

Both obstore and icechunk are built on `object_store`, so this is not only an ingest problem. A virtual chunk that *points* at one of these objects fails at **read** time with the identical error — confirmed end to end against a real icechunk repository:

```
error fetching virtual reference
|-> Generic GCS error: Content-Length Header missing from response
```

A manifest over the flat objects would therefore be unreadable, not merely slow to build.

## Why the documented workaround does not rescue it

Two upstream issues compose:

- [apache/arrow-rs-object-store#774](https://github.com/apache/arrow-rs-object-store/issues/774) — transcoding drops `Content-Length`. Sending `Accept-Encoding: gzip` avoids transcoding, but only below ~8 MiB stored.
- [apache/arrow-rs-object-store#783](https://github.com/apache/arrow-rs-object-store/issues/783) — that header is applied to the OAuth token request too, which then fails.

AFDB objects are 60-95 kB stored, so #774's size limit does not bite and the workaround ought to apply. It does not. Passing `bearer_token` avoids the token fetch #783 breaks, and the read still fails:

```python
store = GCSStore(BUCKET, bearer_token=tok,
                 client_options={"default_headers": {"accept-encoding": "gzip"}})
obstore.get_range(store, "AF-A0A7C3LD06-F1-model_v4.cif", start=0, end=16)
# Generic GCS error: Content-Length Header missing from response
```

Supplying credentials is not a way around this.

## The server is fine

Raw HTTP with the same header against the same object:

```
HTTP/2 206
content-range: bytes 0-15/95204
content-encoding: gzip
content-length: 16
```

Body starts `1f8b`. So GCS honours the range and sends a `Content-Length`; the header is either not reaching the request or not having its intended effect inside `object_store`.

## What it costs us

From `docs/afdb-catalog-cost.md`: addressing the flat objects directly is **$7** for MarinFold's 4.21M entries and finishes in under an hour. The proteome-tar path that works today is **$273-$477**. This issue is worth roughly a fortieth of the build cost.

## What to do

Nothing here for now — the catalog is built from `proteomes/*.tar`, which are `identity` encoding with clean ranged reads. Re-test the three-line reproducer above whenever `object_store` releases; if it passes, the flat-object path becomes available and is dramatically cheaper.

Upstream also has [#806](https://github.com/apache/arrow-rs-object-store/issues/806) (200 response to a whole-object range request), which is adjacent but not what bites here.

Versions tested: obstore 0.11.0, icechunk 2.1.2.
